prompt: Make it look a thousand years old.

card.name: Thousand-Year Hold

site.text: An ordinary settlement on existing land, left open by the player; sited on level or gently rolling ground near the founding stone.

style.text: Look a thousand years old: weathered, mossy, cracked and crumbling stone, overgrown with vines, partly collapsed walls and roofs, worn paths.

purpose.text: A lived-in home base that has endured for ages, with some buildings still in use among the ruins.

card.interpretation: You only gave a mood, so I took "a thousand years old" as the style: weathered ruined stone, moss and vines, partial collapse. The site is a plain village on existing land, the purpose is a home base, and there is no backstory. The program is a medium set of buildings that look ancient and half-fallen, with a few still usable.
assumptions: Size M, medium density, within the 64-block claim.
Site is a village on find terrain, since none was given.
Purpose is a home base, so some buildings remain usable.
Medieval-style architecture underneath the ruin and decay.

program.notes: Half-collapsed hall at the heart, moss-covered stone, broken roof, one wing still sheltered and usable.
Old homes with sagging roofs, mossy cobblestone, vines, and gaps in the walls.
Leaning tower with a broken top, overgrown with ivy.
Roofless nave, cracked windows, a surviving altar.
Cold forge, rusted fittings, collapsed chimney.
Collapsed timber barn at the edge, reclaimed by grass.
Ruined arch marking the entrance, partly fallen.
